facts.title: The Kingdom of Biaineli
facts.text: In the 9th century BCE, Urartu arose as a major power around Lakes Van, Sevan, and Urmia.

facts.title: Tushpa
facts.text: Around 832 BCE, King Sarduri I founded his royal capital at the foot of the Rock of Van.

facts.title: 782 BCE
facts.text: King Argishti I founded the fortress of Erebuni in 782 BCE, the direct ancestor of modern Yerevan.

facts.title: Over 50 km
facts.text: This ancient irrigation network conveyed fresh water to Tushpa and remains in use today.

facts.title: Masters of Metal
facts.text: Using the lost-wax technique, artisans crafted ritual cauldrons, helmets, and engraved shields.

facts.title: Armina
facts.text: Around 520 BCE, King Darius translated the Babylonian name Urashtu as Armina, meaning Armenia.

facts.title: The Legacy of Urartu
facts.text: Its major fortresses saw continuous occupation under the Armenian Orontid dynasty.

ytTitle: Urartu: The Mighty Highland Empire Ancestor to Armenia
ytLead: A sovereign Iron Age power, the Kingdom of Urartu reigned around Lakes Van, Sevan, and Urmia, shaping the cradle of the Armenian Highlands.
